subject: Hosted API vs Dedicated - follow-up & latency/throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API vs Dedicated - follow-up & latency/throughput clarifications

Thanks for the call earlier, Samir — great to learn more about FinPay's flow. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from call:
- FinPay is evaluating Redwood for real-time anti-fraud and KYC enrichment on the payment path.
- Primary constraint: strict P95 latency SLO for inference (target ~250ms or better).
- Current traffic profile: mix of steady RPS with 1-2 daily peaks tied to batch settlements.
- Concern: predictable tail latency during peaks — considering Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity.

Clarifying asks (can you confirm the items below?):
1) Peak and sustained throughput: what are your observed RPS numbers (peak and 5-min sustained)?
2) Average request size: tokens per request (average and 95th)?
3) Any hard latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) or timeouts we should know about?
4) Data residency / VPC needs (are you okay with Hosted in our us-east region, or do you require Private VPC/on-prem?).

High-level tradeoffs we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, simple auth and scaling. Good if your 95th-percentile latency requirement is relaxed (~500ms+ under load), or if you can tolerate occasional slightly higher tail during global spikes.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and lower tail latency. Better if you need consistent P95s ~250ms and have steady committed usage to justify reserved capacity.

Proposed next steps:
- You share peak RPS and token distribution (CSV is fine).
- Neha and Dylan run a quick sizing exercise and propose a Dedicated baseline (GPU count / instance type) and estimated cost.
- Option A: short Hosted PoC (2 weeks) to validate integration.
- Option B: Dedicated pilot (4 weeks) with baseline capacity + load tests to validate P95.

I attached our one-pager that summarizes Hosted vs Dedicated sizing and typical lead times. Once we get the numbers above, we can map to an estimated Dedicated configuration and typical latency expectations.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed workshop time after I have your throughput numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0108

Attachment: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API vs Dedicated - follow-up & latency/throughput clarifications

Thanks Marissa — great meeting. Answers inline below and attached a quick CSV with per-minute RPS from last week (finpay-performance-metrics.csv).

1) Throughput:
- Typical steady: 120 req/sec
- Daily peak (settlement window): 220 req/sec for ~8-12 minutes
- Weekend peak: ~180 req/sec for a few hours

2) Request size:
- Avg tokens/request: ~150 tokens
- 95th percentile: ~420 tokens (some longer enrichment requests)

3) Latency SLOs:
- We target P95 <= 250ms for inline calls (fraud checks). P99 ideally < 500ms.
- Callers will enforce a 1s overall timeout but want to avoid retries at the application layer.

4) Residency / network:
- US-based customers only; us-east region is fine. We prefer dedicated VPC peering for production if we move off Hosted.

Preference: given the tight P95 and the need for predictable tail behavior during the settlement peaks, our infra team leans toward Dedicated capacity, assuming the reservation/lead times and cost make sense.

Next asks from our side:
- Can you provide an estimated sizing (GPU type + count) for 220 peak RPS at ~150 tokens avg and the latency expectation for Hosted vs Dedicated?
- Lead time to spin up Dedicated baseline for a pilot?
- Ballpark pricing for a 3-month pilot vs long-term reserved commitment.

Thanks — I’ve attached the CSV. Happy to jump on a quick technical workshop with Neha & Dylan this week.

—Samir
Head of Engineering | FinPay
samir@finpay.io

Attachment: finpay-performance-metrics.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API vs Dedicated - follow-up & latency/throughput clarifications

Thanks Samir — this is super helpful and exactly what we need. Quick responses and proposed plan: 

Sizing notes (ballpark, subject to workshop validation):
- For ~220 peak RPS at ~150 tokens avg (with headroom for 420-token tail), a Dedicated pool of 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (continuous load balancing + KV cache warm) is likely a reasonable starting baseline to meet P95 ~200-300ms depending on model variant.
- Hosted API with autoscaling could hit similar P50 numbers, but tail/P95 under tight SLOs is harder to guarantee because of multi-tenant cold-starts and noisy neighbors — you’ll generally see higher variance during tight peaks.

Pilot options:
- Dedicated pilot (recommended given your P95 target): 4 GPUs for a 4-week pilot. Redwood will instrument with tracing + per-token cost breakdown and run load tests using your sample CSV.
- Hosted PoC (if you want fastest integration): 2-week integration to validate correctness; we would flag that it may not prove P95 stability at your peak traffic pattern unless we simulate full peak load.

Logistics / lead time:
- Dedicated pilot provisioning: typically 7-10 business days for a new Dedicated pool (depends on region and capacity), or faster if we can reuse an existing cluster.
- Pricing: I’ll send a ballpark estimate in a separate email after Neha sketches the sizing. For pilots we often do a reduced pilot rate and convert to committed reserved pricing if you proceed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical workshop with Neha & Dylan — they’ll run a quick sizing validation and request a sample payload and the CSV you attached (we have it).
2) Neha will provide a benchmark plan (load script + expected P95 curve) and a pilot quote.
3) We schedule the pilot provisioning window once you sign the pilot agreement (DocuSign link to follow).

Samir — what days/times look good for a 60-minute workshop this week? We can do Wed 3-5pm PT or Thu 9-11am PT.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Hi Samir — copying a couple technical details so we can get right to a workshop: 

Immediate asks from engineering to scope the Dedicated pilot: 
- Sample request payloads (1-2 representative requests, including the longer 95th-percentile flow).
- Clarify concurrency model: are calls synchronous inline from your payment path or async enrichment? You indicated inline for fraud checks.
- Any encryption / header auth requirements for peering (we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS).

Technical notes:
- Based on Marissa's rough sizing, we will run an internal benchmark using the exact model you plan to serve (we'll need either the model name or your acceptance to use the open model we've recommended).
- For 220 RPS at ~150 tokens avg: we will prototype a k6 load script and a small harness; expect to run 1-2 hours of incremental ramp tests to validate tail behavior.
- For Dedicated: we can enable isolated pools + pre-warmed KV cache to reduce generation tail latency during peak window. That is the main lever compared to Hosted.

Suggested next actions for the workshop (agenda, 60 min):
1) Walk through FinPay traffic profile & attachments (5-10 min)
2) Review integration pattern and auth/network (10 min)
3) Run through proposed Dedicated sizing and tradeoffs (15 min)
4) Agree on pilot scope & timeline + what success looks like (15 min)
5) Action items and owners (10 min)

Dates we have available: Wed 30 Jun 3-5pm PT, Thu 1 Jul 9-11am PT, Fri 2 Jul 10-12pm PT. Pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite + pre-reqs (sample payload, k6 script template).

-Neha
